title: 28th Sitting of second session of 2026

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/28/2/2026).
Approval of the minutes of three previous sittings (minutes Nos. 22/2/2026 to 24/2/2026).
Announcements from the Chair.
First reading of the Asset Recovery Bill (on property obtained through crime), a government bill submitted by Fuvahmulah Central MP Ali Fazad.
First reading of the bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act (Law No. 12/2016), a government bill submitted by Funadhoo MP Mohamed Mamdhooh.
Committee of the Whole House report on the Bill on Leasing Uninhabited Islands and Lagoons.
Decentralisation Committee report on the President's nomination of two members to the Local Government Authority board from among those designated by Parliament (Decentralization Act, Article 59).
Human Rights and Gender Committee report on the President's nomination of a member to the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives.
Finance Committee report on the Addu City Council secretariat's audit reports for 2012 and 2015 to 2024.
Finance Committee report on the bill to amend the Foreign Currency Act (Law No. 32/2024), after the bill was sent back to the committee for further review.
Economic Committee report on the bill to amend the Maldives Fisheries Act (Law No. 14/2019).
Foreign Relations Committee report on the President's nomination of an ambassador to the United Kingdom.
Independent Institutions Committee report on the President's nominee for Information Commissioner (Right to Information Act, Law No. 1/2014, Article 44).
Economic Committee report on the bill to amend the Tax Administration Act (Law No. 3/2010).
Decentralisation Committee report on the bill to amend the Decentralization Act (Law No. 7/2010).
National Development and Heritage Committee report on the Land Transport Bill.
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.
Any other business.

summary: The last sitting of the second session was a big clean-up day: first readings of two crime-related bills, then eleven committee reports on bills, audits and presidential appointments, followed by votes.
